description: Schema for dtail.json. Property names mirror the JSON-decodable fields of internal/config (CommonConfig, ServerConfig, ClientConfig); internal/config/schema_test.go keeps them in sync. Every section and key is optional: omitted keys keep their built-in defaults. Keys removed from DTail (for example the former TurboBoostDisable and other Turbo*/output tuning keys) are deliberately NOT listed: dtail itself silently ignores unknown keys, but this schema reports them so stale no-op settings can be cleaned up.

loglevel.description: Log level, matched case-insensitively: none, fatal, error, warn, info, default, verbose, debug, devel, trace or all. An empty string is the same as default, which logs more than info (it sits between info and verbose).

logger.description: Logger implementation, matched case-insensitively: none, stdout, file or fout.

logrotation.description: Log rotation strategy, matched case-insensitively: daily or signal. dtail itself treats every value other than daily as signal.

TermColorsEnable.description: Enable terminal colors in client output (default true; --noColor disables).

Remote.description: Colors for lines received from remote servers.

AuthKeyPath.description: Private key whose public half is registered with dserver for auth-key fast reconnect (default ~/.ssh/id_rsa). Overridden by --auth-key-path, DTAIL_AUTH_KEY_PATH and DTAIL_SSH_PRIVATE_KEYFILE_PATH.

LogPayload.description: Tee the full retrieved payload into the daily client log file of the default fout logger (same as --log-payload). Default false: the file keeps diagnostics only; payload always goes to stdout.

SSHBindAddress.description: Address the SSH server binds to.

MaxConnections.description: Maximum number of concurrent user connections.

IdleSessionTimeoutS.description: Rolling inactivity timeout for authenticated SSH sessions, in seconds. Successful reads and writes mark the connection active and a per-connection ticker (interval timeout/4, clamped to 1-30 seconds) refreshes the deadline, so active sessions stay connected. An idle connection closes between timeout + 2 and timeout + 3 intervals after its last activity (about 960-990 seconds at the default). 0 or less uses the 900 second default. Values below about a minute are not useful for log streaming.

MaxConcurrentCats.description: Maximum number of concurrent cat/grep/MapReduce reads per server.

MaxConcurrentTails.description: Maximum number of concurrent tails per server.

MaxLineLength.description: Maximum line length in bytes before a line is split into multiple smaller lines. 0 or less uses the 1 MiB default. The minimum of 1024 is a recommendation of this schema; dserver uses any positive value as is.

Default.description: Permissions of users without an entry in Users (default ["^/.*"]).

Users.description: Per-user permissions; replace Default for that user.

HostKeyFile.description: Deprecated: use HostKeyPath. Legacy private SSH host key path, used only when HostKeyPath is empty.

HostKeyPath.description: Private SSH host key path. When empty, HostKeyFile is used; when both are empty, ./cache/ssh_host_key.

AuthorizedKeysPath.description: One authorized_keys file for all users. When empty, the per-user cache and ~/.ssh/authorized_keys are used.

HostKeyBits.description: RSA host key size in bits when a host key is generated. 0 or less uses 4096. The minimum of 2048 is a recommendation of this schema; dserver does not enforce it.

Files.description: File path or glob of the logs to query. May contain $today, $tomorrow, $yesterday, $yyesterday or $yyyesterday, replaced with the matching YYYYMMDD date before each run.

Outfile.description: Path of the CSV result file. May contain $today, $tomorrow, $yesterday, $yyesterday or $yyyesterday, replaced with the matching YYYYMMDD date before each run.

Discovery.description: Server discovery module: COMMA or FILE (case-insensitive; builds may add more), optionally with options as MODULE:options. It selects how Servers is read: Servers, joined with commas, is the module's input, for example the server list file for FILE. When empty, a Servers value naming an existing file is read as a server list file, otherwise as a comma-separated list.

Servers.description: Servers to query, passed to the Discovery module. When empty, the job queries this dserver's own SSHBindAddress.

AllowFrom.description: Addresses of the dserver instances allowed to connect to run this job.

TimeRange.description: Hours [start, end) of the day during which the job runs.

Files.description: File path or glob of the logs to query. May contain $today, $tomorrow, $yesterday, $yyesterday or $yyyesterday, replaced with the matching YYYYMMDD date before each run.

Outfile.description: Path of the CSV result file. May contain $today, $tomorrow, $yesterday, $yyesterday or $yyyesterday, replaced with the matching YYYYMMDD date before each run.

Discovery.description: Server discovery module: COMMA or FILE (case-insensitive; builds may add more), optionally with options as MODULE:options. It selects how Servers is read: Servers, joined with commas, is the module's input, for example the server list file for FILE. When empty, a Servers value naming an existing file is read as a server list file, otherwise as a comma-separated list.

Servers.description: Servers to query, passed to the Discovery module. When empty, the job queries this dserver's own SSHBindAddress.

AllowFrom.description: Addresses of the dserver instances allowed to connect to run this job.

RestartOnDayChange.description: Restart the job when the day changes.

KeyExchanges.description: Allowed SSH key exchange algorithms. Empty uses the built-in list.

Ciphers.description: Allowed SSH cipher algorithms. Empty uses the built-in list.

MACs.description: Allowed SSH MAC algorithms. Empty uses the built-in list.

AuthKeyEnabled.description: Enable in-memory auth-key registration (AUTHKEY) and fast reconnect.

AuthKeyTTLSeconds.description: Auth-key cache entry TTL in seconds. 0 or less uses the default.

AuthKeyMaxPerUser.description: Maximum number of cached auth keys per user. 0 or less uses the default.

ReadGlobRetryIntervalMs.description: Retry interval for glob retries, in milliseconds. 0 or less uses the default.

ReadRetryIntervalMs.description: Retry interval for re-reading in tail/cat loops, in milliseconds. 0 or less uses the default.

OutputBufferMaxBytes.description: Maximum payload backing memory retained by the output buffer per SSH session; producers apply backpressure at the cap. Must be at least MaxLineLength + 131072 (two 64 KiB writer batches), otherwise dserver refuses the session. 0 or less uses the 2 MiB default.

OutputFlushTimeoutMs.description: Maximum time to wait for the session reader to drain output, in milliseconds. 0 or less uses the default.

OutputReadRetryIntervalMs.description: Compatibility fallback interval, in milliseconds, for detecting a stale generation when an older output writer provides no cancellation signal. Values below the implementation safety minimum are clamped.

OutputEOFAckTimeoutMs.description: Maximum time to wait for the output EOF acknowledgement after signaling EOF, in milliseconds. 0 or less uses the default.

MaxCommandFrameSize.description: Maximum size in bytes of one command frame (bytes between ';' delimiters); a larger frame closes the session. dserver treats 0 or less as no limit for normal sessions (only health-check sessions then fall back to the 1 MiB default); this schema requires at least 1 because disabling the guard lets a client grow a frame without bound.

MaxGlobTargets.description: Maximum number of files one read command's glob may dispatch; excess paths are dropped with a warning. 0 or less uses the default.

Common.description: Settings shared by client and server.

HostnameOverride.description: Replaces the system hostname in logs and output when set.

SSHConnectTimeoutMs.description: Client SSH connection timeout in milliseconds. 0 or less uses the default.

LogDir.description: Log directory. dserver uses this value (default "log", relative to the working directory) unless --logDir is given. The client commands' --logDir flag defaults to ~/log and currently always replaces this value. Every "~/" in the path is replaced with the home directory.

Logger.description: Logger implementation. Note: every command's --logger flag has a non-empty default (clients fout, dserver file, dtailhealth none) that currently replaces this value, so set the flag instead.

LogLevel.description: Maximum log level. An empty string is the same as the level default, which logs more than info (the value this field defaults to). Note: a --logLevel flag other than info replaces this value; dtailhealth's flag defaults to none, so it replaces it unless dtailhealth runs serverless, which always uses warn; a serverless client without --logLevel (or with info) uses warn.
